name: SynthText in the Wild: Synthetic Text Localisation Benchmark
description: SynthText in the Wild is a benchmark dataset and synthetic data generation paradigm for multi-oriented and curved scene text detection in natural images, introduced by Gupta, Vedaldi, and Zisserman at CVPR 2016. Sourced from 8,000 background photographs, SynthText uses dense semantic segmentation and depth maps to realistically render synthetic 3D-oriented text onto suitable planar surfaces. The complete corpus contains 858,750 high-resolution natural scene images containing over 7.2 million synthetic word instances (and ~29 million characters). Unlike word-recognition datasets like MJSynth that supply cropped tokens, SynthText provides full scene images with pixel-precise word and character-level oriented bounding boxes.

provenance.collection_method: Synthetic text projection engine that renders newsgroup text into 8,000 background images using estimated depth and semantic segmentation maps to enforce 3D surface alignment.
